ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.26 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexempted off-route segment's extra mileage, and record the driver's RD-1 breach; refer the driver's account to Ryde review for a repeated upheld route deviation + flag_account.

segment_findings.reason: The 12:12–12:22 segment added 5.15 km with no rider-named stop [F7][F8] (RD-3), no qualifying incident and only band 4–5 speeds [F10][F11][F12] (RD-4), and no pre-deviation driver proposal plus rider agreement [F9] (RD-5); it is an unexempted detour under RD-1, refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's framing of the refundable sum as the whole billed excess is trimmed by RD-2: for a RydeTAXI trip only the unexempted segment's mileage units are refundable, computed from the fare rate [F6][F4] (RD-2); base, time and platform components are not mileage units.

The absence of a stop or waiting charge [F6] and fair weather [F13] do not by themselves establish the deviation; liability rests on the unexplained off-route segment [F3] under RD-1, with RD-3 merely failing to provide an exemption.

The driver's attempt to cap exposure at residue rather than the segment is only partly right: the ~0.75 km map-matching residue is indeed non-refundable [F1][F3], but the full 5.15 km segment extra remains refundable and is not reduced by RD-2 (RD-2).

The driver's 3.4-year, 1093-trip, 4.61-rating history and the rider's clean record [F14][F15] cannot offset an established RD-1 breach; profile facts never decide liability and only bear on the RD-6 add-on (RD-6).

The rider's headline distance is indeed overstated [F1][F6], but that does not defeat the claim: it merely confines recovery to the segment's mileage units under RD-2 (RD-2), which the driver himself concedes at $7.26.
